title: Integral rho section modules are self-dual at the admissible weights
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and algebraically closed residue field $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$. Let $H$ be a smooth affine finitely presented group scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with the group-object diagrams over this base. Suppose $H$ is split semisimple simply connected: its geometric fibres are connected and have no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, every central isogeny onto such a fibre from a connected semisimple group is an isomorphism, and choose a split maximal torus $T\subseteq H$ and a Borel subgroup scheme $B\supseteq T$. Here a central isogeny is a surjective group homomorphism with finite central kernel; solvable means that the iterated derived subgroups eventually become trivial; a split torus is a group scheme isomorphic to a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$; maximal tori and Borel subgroup schemes have, on each geometric fibre, a maximal torus and a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup, respectively. Write $\mathbf G_m(C)=C^\times$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $C$. A character is a homomorphism of group schemes to $\mathbf G_m$. Let $\Phi^+$ be the positive roots determined by $B$, namely the nonzero characters occurring in the adjoint $T$-action on $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$; the latter is the tangent module at the identity, defined by dual-number points reducing to the identity. In the character lattice $X^*(T)$, addition means multiplication of character values. Use the rational section modules of [lem-sfb-dvr-rho-section-modules], with the following explicit description. Let $\rho\in X^*(T)$ satisfy $2\rho=\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$, and let $\widetilde\rho:B\to\mathbf G_m$ extend $\rho$ and be trivial on the unipotent radical of $B$. This radical is the subgroup whose geometric fibres are the largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroups; unipotent means that all geometric points become unipotent matrices in a faithful linear representation. For every integer $m\ge1$, put $$W_m=\{f\in A[H]:f(gb)=\widetilde\rho(b)^m f(g)\text{ for all commutative }A\text{-algebras }C,\ g\in H(C),\ b\in B(C)\}.$$ Evaluation of $f$ means pullback of the regular function along its $C$-point. Use the left-translation action $(h f)(g)=f(h^{-1}g)$. A rational $H$-module is an $A$-module $M$ with an $A$-linear coaction $M\to M\otimes_A A[H]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities, where $A[H]=\Gamma(H,\mathcal O_H)$ is the coordinate Hopf algebra. Its invariants are $M^H=\{x:\rho_M(x)=x\otimes1\}$. Equivariant maps commute with coactions; tensor products have diagonal coaction. These identities are tested after every commutative $A$-algebra extension, not just on $A$-points. Write $W_m^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(W_m,A)$, with contragredient action $(h\ell)(w)=\ell(h^{-1}w)$ after every scalar extension. If $\operatorname{char}\kappa=0$, then for every $m\ge1$ there is an equivariant $A$-linear isomorphism $W_m\simeq W_m^\vee$. If $\operatorname{char}\kappa=p>0$, then for every integer $r\ge1$ and $m=p^r-1$ there is an equivariant $A$-linear isomorphism $W_m\simeq W_m^\vee$.

proof.text: Fix an allowed $m$ and put $W=W_m$, $V=W\otimes_A\kappa$, $G=H_\kappa$. By [lem-sfb-dvr-rho-section-modules], $W$ is finite free of positive rank, hence $V$ is a nonzero finite-dimensional rational $G$-module. The DVR is a nonzero Noetherian local ring by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] and [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. Its semisimple geometric fibres are reductive: a smooth connected unipotent normal subgroup is solvable by [lem-sfb-smooth-unipotent-solvable], hence trivial. Apply [lem-sfb-local-borel-quotient-geometry] to the chosen split torus and Borel pair. Its root-comparison and radical-base-change clauses identify $\rho_\kappa$ with the half-sum for $T_\kappa\subseteq B_\kappa$ and make $\widetilde\rho_\kappa$ trivial on the fibre's unipotent radical. Write $S_m$ for the actual $\kappa[G]$ section module with exponent $m\rho_\kappa$. It is nonzero finite-dimensional and rational by [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules].

proof.text: Let $R=A[H]$, $D=A[B]$ and choose a uniformizer $\pi$ as in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Both $H$ and its Borel subgroup scheme $B$ are smooth over $A$. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine], $R$ and $D$ are flat $A$-modules. Since $A$ is a domain and $\pi\ne0$, [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] applied to $A\xrightarrow{\pi}A$ gives injectivity of multiplication by $\pi$ on $R$ and $D$. Apply that same definition with the injection $D\xrightarrow{\pi}D$ and the flat module $R$: multiplication by $\pi$ is injective on $R\otimes_A D$. It is also injective on $(W\otimes_AW)\otimes_AR$, a finite direct sum of copies of $R$ in the tensor basis. These are the only cancellation assertions needed below.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the right action of $B$ gives $u:R\to R\otimes_AD$ with $u(f)(g,b)=f(gb)$ and character function $z=\widetilde\rho\in D^\times$. Universal affine points identify $W=\ker d$, where $d(f)=u(f)-f\otimes z^m$. If $w\in W$ has zero reduction in $R/\pi R$, write $w=\pi f$ with $f\in R$. Then $0=d(w)=\pi d(f)$, so Step 2 gives $d(f)=0$, hence $f\in W$. Therefore $W\cap\pi R=\pi W$. Identifying $W\otimes_A\kappa=W/\pi W$ by reduction of coordinates, the reduction map gives an injection $j:V\hookrightarrow R/\pi R=\kappa[G]$. The same affine-product formula puts its image in $S_m$, and left translation $f(h^{-1}g)$ commutes with reduction, so $j:V\hookrightarrow S_m$ is equivariant as a coaction map. No surjectivity of $j$ has been assumed.

proof.text: Suppose $\operatorname{char}\kappa=0$. In [lem-sfb-induced-module-primitive-line], take $E_B(-m\rho_\kappa)=S_m$; its invariant-line clause gives $\dim S_m^{U_\kappa}=1$. By [lem-sfb-characteristic-zero-complete-reducibility], $S_m$ is a finite direct sum of simple rational $G$-modules. Each summand has a one-dimensional $U_\kappa$-fixed line by [lem-sfb-simple-module-dual-highest-weight]. The coaction on a direct sum is componentwise, so invariants commute with this finite sum and there is exactly one summand. Thus $S_m$ is simple. Step 3 embeds the nonzero $V$ equivariantly into it; its image must be all of $S_m$. Hence $V$ is simple. This use of simplicity to deduce surjectivity occurs only after the injectivity argument.

proof.text: Suppose $\operatorname{char}\kappa=p>0$ and $m=p^r-1$. Use $G,T_\kappa,B_\kappa,\rho_\kappa$ in [lem-sfb-steinberg-infinitesimal-restriction-injective]: all its field, semisimplicity, simple-connectedness, torus, Borel and half-sum hypotheses hold by the item and Step 1. It embeds $S_m$ by restriction into the actual rational $L_r=G_rT_\kappa$-module $Z_r$. That module is simple by [lem-sfb-steinberg-infinitesimal-induced-simple], with exactly the same Frobenius preimage $L_r$, subgroup $P_r$, positive exponent and translation action. Compose with $j$ from Step 3. The image of $V$ is a nonzero rational $L_r$-submodule of $Z_r$, so it is all of $Z_r$; hence $V$ restricted to $L_r$ is simple. Every rational $G$-submodule of $V$ is also an $L_r$-submodule, by composing its coaction with $\kappa[G]\to\kappa[L_r]$. Thus $V$ is simple as a rational $G$-module. This argument uses no Weyl dimension, integral section-base-change surjectivity or Kempf vanishing.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-dvr-rho-tensor-square-invariant-line], $L=(W\otimes_AW)^H$ is free of rank one; choose a generator $t$. If $t=\pi s$ in $W\otimes_AW$, its invariance gives $\pi(c(s)-s\otimes1)=0$. Step 2 forces $c(s)=s\otimes1$, so $s\in L$ and $s=a t$ for some $a\in A$. Then $(1-\pi a)t=0$, impossible because $t$ is a basis of $L$ and $1-\pi a$ is a unit in the local ring. Hence $t$ is not divisible by $\pi$ and its reduction $\bar t\in V\otimes_\kappa V$ is nonzero, as the kernel of reduction in the tensor basis is $\pi(W\otimes_AW)$. This proves primitivity without any assertion that invariants commute with reduction.

proof.text: Write $t=\sum_i x_i\otimes y_i$ and define $\theta:W^\vee\to W$ by $\theta(\ell)=\sum_i\ell(x_i)y_i$. A finite basis identifies this contraction with the matrix whose entries are the coefficients of $t$ in the tensor basis. Invariance of $t$ gives equivariance: for every commutative $A$-algebra $C$ and $h\in H(C)$, replace $t$ by $\sum_i hx_i\otimes hy_i$ to obtain $\theta(h\ell)=\sum_i(h\ell)(hx_i)hy_i=h\theta(\ell)$. These are universal coaction identities. Under the dual-basis identification $W^\vee\otimes\kappa=V^\vee$, reduction of $\theta$ is the contraction by $\bar t$, which is nonzero by Step 6. Its image is a nonzero rational submodule of the simple module $V$, so it is all of $V$. The source and target have the same finite dimension, so $\bar\theta$ is invertible. Consequently $\det\theta$ has nonzero residue, hence is a unit in the local ring $A$. The adjugate formula gives an inverse over $A$. Inverting the equivariance identity makes $\theta^{-1}:W\xrightarrow{\sim}W^\vee$ equivariant after every scalar extension. This proves both asserted characteristic cases.
